name: Sicilian Defense: Najdorf
desc: The sharpest and most respected answer to 1.e4, played by Fischer and Kasparov. The little move 5...a6 keeps every option open. Learn Black's plans against the English Attack, 6.Bg5, 6.Be2, the Sozin 6.Bc4, 6.f3, 6.h3 and the early Bb5+ and Qxd4 deviations.

lines.name: English Attack 6.Be3
lines.moves: 1.e4 c5 {The Sicilian: fighting for d4 from the side.} 2.Nf3 d6 3.d4 cxd4 {Trading a wing pawn for a center pawn.} 4.Nxd4 Nf6 {Hitting e4 to force Nc3.} 5.Nc3 a6 {The Najdorf: controlling b5 and preparing ...e5 or ...b5.} 6.Be3 e5 {Gaining space and kicking the knight.} 7.Nb3 Be6 8.f3 Be7 9.Qd2 O-O 10.O-O-O Nbd7 11.g4 b5 {Opposite-side castling: a pure race of pawn storms.}

lines.name: Main line 6.Bg5
lines.moves: 1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 d6 3.d4 cxd4 4.Nxd4 Nf6 5.Nc3 a6 6.Bg5 e6 {Solid: preparing ...Be7 and unpinning.} 7.f4 Be7 8.Qf3 Qc7 9.O-O-O Nbd7 10.g4 b5 {Black's queenside counterattack starts.}

lines.name: Classical 6.Be2
lines.moves: 1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 d6 3.d4 cxd4 4.Nxd4 Nf6 5.Nc3 a6 6.Be2 e5 7.Nb3 Be7 8.O-O O-O 9.Be3 Be6 10.Qd2 Nbd7 {A healthy position; Black aims for ...b5 and ...d5.}

lines.name: Sozin 6.Bc4
lines.moves: 1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 d6 3.d4 cxd4 4.Nxd4 Nf6 5.Nc3 a6 6.Bc4 e6 {Blunting the bishop.} 7.Bb3 b5 8.O-O Be7 9.Qf3 Qc7 10.Qg3 O-O 11.Bh6 Ne8 {Black holds g7 and keeps a solid position.}

lines.name: 6.f3
lines.moves: 1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 d6 3.d4 cxd4 4.Nxd4 Nf6 5.Nc3 a6 6.f3 e5 7.Nb3 Be6 8.Be3 Be7 9.Qd2 O-O 10.O-O-O Nbd7 {Same plans as the English Attack.}

lines.name: Adams Attack 6.h3
lines.moves: 1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 d6 3.d4 cxd4 4.Nxd4 Nf6 5.Nc3 a6 6.h3 e5 7.Nde2 h5 {Stopping White's g4 expansion.}

lines.name: Moscow 3.Bb5+
lines.moves: 1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 d6 3.Bb5+ {Avoiding the Open Sicilian.} Bd7 4.Bxd7+ Qxd7 5.O-O Nc6 6.c3 Nf6 7.Re1 e6 8.d4 cxd4 9.cxd4 d5 {Hitting the center: equal and solid.}

lines.name: Chekhover 4.Qxd4
lines.moves: 1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 d6 3.d4 cxd4 4.Qxd4 {An early queen recapture.} Nc6 {Gaining time on the queen.} 5.Bb5 Bd7 6.Bxc6 Bxc6 7.Nc3 Nf6 8.Bg5 e6 9.O-O-O Be7 {Black has the bishop pair.}

name: Sicilian Defense: Dragon
desc: Black fianchettoes the bishop on g7 where it breathes fire down the long diagonal. Learn the modern antidote to the Yugoslav Attack (9.O-O-O d5), the 9.Bc4 main line, plus the Classical, Levenfish and Fianchetto systems.

lines.name: Yugoslav Attack 9.Bc4
lines.moves: 1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 d6 3.d4 cxd4 4.Nxd4 Nf6 5.Nc3 g6 {The Dragon.} 6.Be3 Bg7 7.f3 O-O 8.Qd2 Nc6 9.Bc4 Bd7 10.O-O-O Rc8 {Rook to the open c-file.} 11.Bb3 Ne5 12.Kb1 Nc4 {Trading off the dangerous bishop.}

lines.name: Yugoslav Attack 9.O-O-O d5!
lines.moves: 1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 d6 3.d4 cxd4 4.Nxd4 Nf6 5.Nc3 g6 6.Be3 Bg7 7.f3 O-O 8.Qd2 Nc6 9.O-O-O d5! {The modern antidote: strike in the center immediately.} 10.exd5 Nxd5 11.Nxc6 bxc6 12.Bd4 e5 13.Bc5 Be6 {Black has great activity for the pawn structure.}

lines.name: Classical 6.Be2
lines.moves: 1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 d6 3.d4 cxd4 4.Nxd4 Nf6 5.Nc3 g6 6.Be2 Bg7 7.O-O O-O 8.Be3 Nc6 9.Nb3 Be6 10.f4 Qc8 {Pressure on the c-file and ...Bc4 ideas.}

lines.name: Levenfish 6.f4
lines.moves: 1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 d6 3.d4 cxd4 4.Nxd4 Nf6 5.Nc3 g6 6.f4 Nbd7 {Preventing the e5 push.} 7.Nf3 Bg7 8.Bd3 O-O 9.O-O Nc5 {Active knight, hitting d3 and e4.}

lines.name: Fianchetto 6.g3
lines.moves: 1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 d6 3.d4 cxd4 4.Nxd4 Nf6 5.Nc3 g6 6.g3 Nc6 7.Nde2 Bg7 8.Bg2 O-O 9.O-O Rb8 {Preparing ...b5 queenside expansion.}

name: Sicilian: Beating the Anti-Sicilians
desc: Not everyone allows the Open Sicilian. Learn how to meet the Alapin, the Smith-Morra Gambit, the Grand Prix, the Closed Sicilian, the Wing Gambit and the Bowdler Attack.

lines.name: Alapin 2.c3
lines.moves: 1.e4 c5 2.c3 {The Alapin: preparing d4.} Nf6 {Hitting e4 at once.} 3.e5 Nd5 4.d4 cxd4 5.Nf3 Nc6 6.cxd4 d6 7.Bc4 Nb6 8.Bb5 dxe5 9.Nxe5 Bd7 {Black has a comfortable game.}

lines.name: Smith-Morra Gambit
lines.moves: 1.e4 c5 2.d4 cxd4 3.c3 {The Smith-Morra Gambit.} dxc3 {Accepting is perfectly fine.} 4.Nxc3 Nc6 5.Nf3 d6 6.Bc4 e6 {Blunting the bishop and closing the a2-g8 diagonal.} 7.O-O Nf6 8.Qe2 Be7 9.Rd1 e5 {Stopping the e5 break; Black keeps the extra pawn.}

lines.name: Grand Prix Attack
lines.moves: 1.e4 c5 2.Nc3 Nc6 3.f4 {The Grand Prix Attack.} g6 4.Nf3 Bg7 5.Bc4 e6 {Blunting the c4 bishop; ...Nge7 and ...d5 follow.}

lines.name: Grand Prix 5.Bb5
lines.moves: 1.e4 c5 2.Nc3 Nc6 3.f4 g6 4.Nf3 Bg7 5.Bb5 Nd4 {Avoiding doubled pawns and centralizing.}

lines.name: Closed Sicilian
lines.moves: 1.e4 c5 2.Nc3 Nc6 3.g3 g6 4.Bg2 Bg7 5.d3 d6 6.Be3 e5 {The Botvinnik setup: a firm grip on d4.}

lines.name: Closed: 3.Bb5
lines.moves: 1.e4 c5 2.Nc3 Nc6 3.Bb5 Nd4 {Avoiding doubled pawns and gaining time on the bishop.}

lines.name: Wing Gambit 2.b4?!
lines.moves: 1.e4 c5 2.b4?! {The Wing Gambit: dubious.} cxb4 3.a3 d5! {Return to the center!} 4.exd5 Qxd5 5.Nf3 e5 6.axb4 Bxb4 {Black has an excellent position.}

lines.name: Bowdler Attack 2.Bc4?!
lines.moves: 1.e4 c5 2.Bc4?! {The bishop will be hit by ...d5.} e6 3.Nf3 d5 4.exd5 exd5 5.Bb5+ Nc6 {Black has a free and active position.}

name: French Defense
desc: A resilient counter-attacking defense: Black builds a pawn chain and strikes White's center with ...c5 and ...f6. Learn the Advance, Exchange, Tarrasch, Winawer (including the Poisoned Pawn) and the King's Indian Attack.

lines.name: Advance Variation
lines.moves: 1.e4 e6 {The French: preparing ...d5.} 2.d4 d5 3.e5 {The Advance: gaining space.} c5 {Strike the base of the pawn chain!} 4.c3 Nc6 5.Nf3 Qb6 {Maximum pressure on d4.} 6.a3 c4 {Gaining queenside space and fixing b2.} 7.Nbd2 Na5 {Heading for b3.}

lines.name: Advance: Milner-Barry Gambit
lines.moves: 1.e4 e6 2.d4 d5 3.e5 c5 4.c3 Nc6 5.Nf3 Qb6 6.Bd3!? {The Milner-Barry Gambit.} cxd4 7.cxd4 Bd7! {Careful: 7...Nxd4?? 8.Nxd4 Qxd4?? 9.Bb5+ wins the queen.}

lines.name: Exchange Variation
lines.moves: 1.e4 e6 2.d4 d5 3.exd5 exd5 {Symmetrical, but Black can play for a win.} 4.Bd3 Nc6 5.c3 Bd6 6.Nf3 Nge7 7.O-O Bg4 {Active and comfortable.}

lines.name: Tarrasch 3.Nd2
lines.moves: 1.e4 e6 2.d4 d5 3.Nd2 c5 {The most direct answer.} 4.exd5 Qxd5 5.Ngf3 cxd4 6.Bc4 Qd6 7.O-O Nf6 8.Nb3 Nc6 9.Nbxd4 Nxd4 10.Nxd4 a6 {Main line: Black is solid.}

lines.name: Winawer: Poisoned Pawn
lines.moves: 1.e4 e6 2.d4 d5 3.Nc3 Bb4 {The Winawer: pinning the knight.} 4.e5 c5 5.a3 Bxc3+ 6.bxc3 Ne7 7.Qg4 Qc7 {Counter-attack instead of defending g7.} 8.Qxg7 Rg8 9.Qxh7 cxd4 10.Ne2 Nbc6 11.f4 dxc3 {The Poisoned Pawn: wild and double-edged.}

lines.name: Winawer: 7.Nf3 positional
lines.moves: 1.e4 e6 2.d4 d5 3.Nc3 Bb4 4.e5 c5 5.a3 Bxc3+ 6.bxc3 Ne7 7.Nf3 Nbc6 8.a4 Qa5 9.Qd2 Bd7 10.Be2 f6 {Undermining the e5 pawn.}

lines.name: Exchange Winawer 4.exd5
lines.moves: 1.e4 e6 2.d4 d5 3.Nc3 Bb4 4.exd5 exd5 5.Bd3 Nc6 6.a3 Bxc3+ 7.bxc3 Nge7 {Black is fine with easy development.}

lines.name: King's Indian Attack 2.d3
lines.moves: 1.e4 e6 2.d3 d5 3.Nd2 Nf6 4.Ngf3 c5 5.g3 Nc6 6.Bg2 Be7 7.O-O O-O {Solid; Black will expand on the queenside.}

name: Caro-Kann Defense
desc: Solid and reliable: Black supports ...d5 with ...c6 and gets the light-squared bishop out before ...e6. Learn the Advance, Classical, Exchange, Panov, Two Knights and Fantasy variations.

lines.name: Advance: Short System
lines.moves: 1.e4 c6 {The Caro-Kann: preparing ...d5.} 2.d4 d5 3.e5 {The Advance Variation.} Bf5 {The bishop gets out before ...e6.} 4.Nf3 e6 5.Be2 c5 {Striking the center.} 6.Be3 Nd7 7.O-O Ne7 {Heading for c6 or g6.}

lines.name: Advance: 4.Bd3?! trade
lines.moves: 1.e4 c6 2.d4 d5 3.e5 Bf5 4.Bd3?! {Offering a bishop trade, but in the Caro-Kann this bishop is Black's good piece and the trade only helps Black develop.} Bxd3 5.Qxd3 e6 {Black has traded off the light bishop and is very comfortable.}

lines.name: Classical 4...Bf5
lines.moves: 1.e4 c6 2.d4 d5 3.Nc3 dxe4 4.Nxe4 Bf5 {The Classical Caro-Kann.} 5.Ng3 Bg6 6.h4 h6 {Keeping the bishop safe.} 7.Nf3 Nd7 8.h5 Bh7 9.Bd3 Bxd3 10.Qxd3 e6 11.Bd2 Ngf6 12.O-O-O Be7 {Solid main line.}

lines.name: Exchange Variation
lines.moves: 1.e4 c6 2.d4 d5 3.exd5 cxd5 4.Bd3 Nc6 5.c3 Nf6 6.Bf4 Bg4 {Developing the bishop outside the pawn chain.} 7.Qb3 Qd7 8.Nd2 e6 {A healthy Carlsbad structure.}

lines.name: Panov Attack
lines.moves: 1.e4 c6 2.d4 d5 3.exd5 cxd5 4.c4 {The Panov: an isolated queen pawn position.} Nf6 5.Nc3 e6 6.Nf3 Be7 7.cxd5 Nxd5 8.Bd3 Nc6 9.O-O O-O {Black blockades d5 and targets the isolated pawn.}

lines.name: Two Knights 2.Nc3
lines.moves: 1.e4 c6 2.Nc3 d5 3.Nf3 Bg4 {Pinning the knight.} 4.h3 Bxf3 5.Qxf3 e6 6.d4 Nf6 7.Bd3 dxe4 8.Bxe4 Nxe4 9.Qxe4 Nd7 {Solid and equal.}

lines.name: Fantasy 3.f3
lines.moves: 1.e4 c6 2.d4 d5 3.f3 {The Fantasy Variation.} e6 4.Nc3 Bb4 5.a3 Bxc3+ 6.bxc3 dxe4 7.fxe4 Qh4+! {Exploiting the weakened kingside.} 8.Ke2 Qxe4+ 9.Kf2 Qh4+ 10.g3 Qd8 {A clean extra pawn and an exposed white king.}

name: Scandinavian Defense
desc: Black challenges e4 on move one. After 2.exd5 Qxd5 3.Nc3 the queen retreats to a5 and Black develops harmoniously with ...Nf6, ...Bf5, ...c6 and ...e6. Learn the main lines and how to handle 2.e5 and 2.Nc3.

lines.name: Main line 3...Qa5
lines.moves: 1.e4 d5 {The Scandinavian: challenging e4 right away.} 2.exd5 Qxd5 3.Nc3 Qa5 {The queen is safe here and pins the knight.} 4.d4 Nf6 5.Nf3 Bf5 {Developing the bishop outside the chain.} 6.Bc4 e6 7.Bd2 c6 {A solid triangle: Black has a very healthy position.}

lines.name: 3.Nf3 avoiding Nc3
lines.moves: 1.e4 d5 2.exd5 Qxd5 3.Nf3 Nf6 4.d4 Bg4 {Pinning the knight.} 5.Be2 e6 6.O-O Nc6 7.c4 Qa5 {Flexible development.}

lines.name: 3.d4 central
lines.moves: 1.e4 d5 2.exd5 Qxd5 3.d4 Nf6 4.Nf3 Bf5 5.c4 Qa5+ {The check disrupts White's development.}

lines.name: Gambit 4.b4?!
lines.moves: 1.e4 d5 2.exd5 Qxd5 3.Nc3 Qa5 4.b4?! {A tricky gambit.} Qxb4 5.Rb1 Qd6 {Black keeps the pawn and the queen is safe.}

lines.name: Advance 2.e5
lines.moves: 1.e4 d5 2.e5 Bf5 {A French structure, but with the good bishop already outside.} 3.d4 e6 {Very comfortable for Black.}

lines.name: 2.Nc3 d4
lines.moves: 1.e4 d5 2.Nc3 d4 {Gaining space with tempo.} 3.Nce2 e5 {A big center for Black.}

name: Alekhine's Defense
desc: A provocative hypermodern defense: Black invites White's pawns forward, then attacks the over-extended center. Learn the Modern, Four Pawns, Exchange and Chase variations.

lines.name: Modern 4.Nf3
lines.moves: 1.e4 Nf6 {Alekhine's Defense: provoking e5.} 2.e5 Nd5 3.d4 d6 {Attacking the e5 pawn at once.} 4.Nf3 Bg4 5.Be2 e6 6.O-O Be7 7.h3 Bh5 8.c4 Nb6 9.Nc3 O-O 10.Be3 d5 {Main line: Black fixes the center and targets c4.}

lines.name: Modern 5.h3?! Bxf3
lines.moves: 1.e4 Nf6 2.e5 Nd5 3.d4 d6 4.Nf3 Bg4 5.h3?! Bxf3 6.Qxf3 dxe5 7.dxe5 e6 {Black is fine and e5 is weak.}

lines.name: Four Pawns Attack
lines.moves: 1.e4 Nf6 2.e5 Nd5 3.d4 d6 4.c4 Nb6 5.f4 {The Four Pawns Attack: maximum space.} dxe5 6.fxe5 Nc6 7.Be3 Bf5 8.Nc3 e6 9.Nf3 Be7 {Black targets the over-extended center.}

lines.name: Exchange Variation
lines.moves: 1.e4 Nf6 2.e5 Nd5 3.d4 d6 4.c4 Nb6 5.exd6 cxd6 6.Nc3 g6 7.Be3 Bg7 8.Rc1 O-O {Black has a comfortable hypermodern setup.}

lines.name: Chase Variation 3.c4
lines.moves: 1.e4 Nf6 2.e5 Nd5 3.c4 Nb6 4.c5 Nd5 5.Bc4 e6 6.Nc3 d6 7.cxd6 cxd6 {Black has a solid position.}

lines.name: 2.Nc3 e5
lines.moves: 1.e4 Nf6 2.Nc3 e5 {Transposing to an Open Game.} 3.Nf3 Nc6 {The Four Knights.}

name: Pirc Defense
desc: Black allows White a big center, fianchettoes the bishop and counter-attacks later. Learn the Austrian Attack, the 150 Attack, the Classical system and how to punish an early e5 push.

lines.name: Austrian Attack 5...c5
lines.moves: 1.e4 d6 2.d4 Nf6 {Hitting e4.} 3.Nc3 g6 {The Pirc.} 4.f4 Bg7 5.Nf3 c5 {Striking at the center immediately.} 6.dxc5 Qa5 7.Bd3 Qxc5 8.Qe2 O-O 9.Be3 Qa5 10.O-O Bg4 {Main line: Black has active pieces.}

lines.name: Austrian 5.e5?!
lines.moves: 1.e4 d6 2.d4 Nf6 3.Nc3 g6 4.f4 Bg7 5.e5?! {Premature.} Nfd7 6.Nf3 c5 {Undermining the center.}

lines.name: 150 Attack 4.Be3
lines.moves: 1.e4 d6 2.d4 Nf6 3.Nc3 g6 4.Be3 Bg7 5.Qd2 c6 6.f3 b5 {Queenside counterplay.} 7.Nge2 Nbd7 8.Bh6 Bxh6 9.Qxh6 Bb7 {Black prepares ...e5 or ...c5.}

lines.name: Classical 4.Nf3
lines.moves: 1.e4 d6 2.d4 Nf6 3.Nc3 g6 4.Nf3 Bg7 5.Be2 O-O 6.O-O c6 7.a4 a5 {Securing b4 for a knight.} 8.h3 Na6 {Heading for b4.}
